secrets.write: Not written: it looks like a secret ({hits}). Read it from an environment variable or a secret store instead. {hint}
secrets.commit: The staged changes contain what looks like a secret: {hits}. Remove it and commit again. {hint}
secrets.commitFile: These files must not be committed: {files}. Unstage them and add them to .gitignore.
protected.write: Not writing to {why} ({file}). Let the user fill in secrets; for an example, create a value-less file such as .env.example.
size.write: The new file has {lines} lines, over the limit of {max}. Split it by responsibility. {hint}
unsafeHtml.write: Inserts text as HTML or runs a string as code: {hits}. Use textContent for text; if HTML is truly needed, escape it or pass it through a sanitizer such as DOMPurify. Do not use eval or new Function. {hint}
pinDeps.write: Dependency versions are ranges: {hits}. Pin exact versions (e.g. 1.2.3). Install with `npm install --save-exact` (`--exact` for pnpm, yarn, bun) or set `save-exact=true` in .npmrc.
gha.run: {hits} is put straight into `run:` (an issue title or branch name can inject commands). Pass it through `env:` and use "$VAR" in the script.
gha.prt: `pull_request_target` checks out the PR's code ({hits}), running untrusted code with write access and secrets. Use `pull_request`, or do not check out the PR head.
gha.pin: Third-party actions are not pinned to a commit: {hits}. Use the full 40-character commit SHA (e.g. `owner/repo@<sha> # v1.2.3`); tags can be moved.
history.amend: HEAD is already pushed ({remote}), so do not amend it. Add the fix as a new commit.
history.rebase: This rebase rewrites commits that are already pushed ({remote}). Do not rewrite pushed history; merge the latest changes or fix with a new commit.
prMerge.missing: `gh pr merge` is missing {missing}. Squash into one commit and delete the merged branch: `gh pr merge <number> --squash --delete-branch`.
danger.cmd: Blocked an irreversible, dangerous command (wiping the system or home, piping a downloaded script into a shell, 777 permissions, ...). If it is really needed, ask the user to run it themselves.
danger.discard: This command discards {count} uncommitted change(s). Run `git stash` first or confirm with the user.
password.cli: Do not put passwords on the command line (they stay in shell history and process lists). Use --password-stdin, a file, or an environment variable reference ($VAR).
git.addAll: Do not use `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git add *` or `git add -u` without paths. Add only the files you changed for this task.
git.commitAll: Do not use `git commit -a`. Add the files you changed, then commit.
git.protectedCommit: Do not commit directly to the protected branch ({branch}). Create one with `git switch -c feature/<name>`, commit there and merge through a PR.
git.protectedPick: Do not commit directly to the protected branch ({branch}) with `git {sub}`. Create a branch with `git switch -c fix/<name>`, run {sub} there and merge it (merges are not blocked).
git.protectedForce: Do not force-push to a protected branch. Fix things with a new commit instead of rewriting pushed history.
git.protectedDelete: Do not delete the protected branch ({branch}) on the remote. If it really has to go, ask the user to do it themselves.
git.protectedPush: Do not push directly to a protected branch. Push a feature branch and open a PR.
git.msgConventional: Commit message is not in `type: description` form ("{subject}"). e.g. `feat: add login`, `fix(api): handle empty response`. Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert.
git.msgLong: Commit subject is {len} characters (max {max}). Put details in the body after a blank line.
git.branchName: Branch name `{name}` does not match the convention. e.g. {examples} (pattern: {pattern})
git.branchNameNoExample: Branch name `{name}` does not match the convention. (pattern: {pattern})
git.noVerify: Do not skip pre-commit checks with `--no-verify` (or `git commit -n`). Fix what the check reports instead.
web.preferGh: Read GitHub ({url}) with `gh` instead of scraping the page, e.g. `gh repo view`, `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>`, `gh issue view`.
config.broken: harness-fit: {file} is not valid JSON or has the wrong shape (rules must be an object), so all hooks are off. Fix it or re-apply with /harness-fit:setup.
hook.crashed: harness-fit: a hook crashed, so this action runs without hooks. If it keeps happening, re-apply with /harness-fit:setup or update the plugin.
hook.ruleCrashed: harness-fit: the {ids} hook crashed, so this action runs without it. If it keeps happening, re-apply with /harness-fit:setup or update the plugin.
commit.prefix: Found in the changes to be committed —
gitHook.howToFix: Fix it, git add again and commit (stopped by the harness-fit git pre-commit hook).
gitHook.error: Could not run the pre-commit check, so it was skipped.
gitHook.ruleCrashed: The {ids} hook crashed, so this commit goes ahead without it.
commit.unseen: An earlier part of this command ({part}) can change the files being committed, so the pre-commit check cannot see what will go in. Run the command that creates or edits files first, then run git add and git commit separately.
git.msgUnseen: Could not read the commit message from the command (it comes from another command or a file made in the same command), so its format was not checked. Write the message with -m, or create the message file first and commit in a separate command.
git.noVerifyEnv: Not turning off pre-commit checks with the {name} environment variable. If a check fails, fix the cause.
git.hooksPath: Not skipping pre-commit checks by changing core.hooksPath. If the hooks folder really must change, ask the user to do it.
allow.hint: If it is safe for a clear reason, add `lint:allow {id} <reason>` at the end of the line or in a comment line right above it (reason of {min}+ characters; the user is told every time).
allow.hintTop: If it really must stay one file, add a `lint:allow {id} <reason>` comment within the first {top} lines (reason of {min}+ characters; the user is told every time).
allow.secretsOff: If it is not a secret, tell the user. The secrets hook does not accept allow comments by default (once the user turns on the hook option "Accept allow comments", `lint:allow secrets <reason>` works).
allow.noReason: The `lint:allow {id}` comment was ignored because its reason is missing or too short. Write a reason of {min}+ characters.
allow.used: harness-fit: lines passed by allow comments — {list}
swift-unsafe.write: Not written: new Swift lines contain {hits}. try! crashes the app on failure — handle it with do/catch or try?. print stays in release builds and leaks paths and values — use os.Logger with privacy levels. {hint}
python-unsafe.write: Not written: new Python lines contain {hits}. shell=True runs any value mixed into the command through the shell — pass an argument list (["git", "log", name]). eval/exec run text as code — for values use ast.literal_eval or json.loads. {hint}
push.squash: {branch} has {n} commits that are not on any remote yet. One piece of work goes up as one commit: run `git reset --soft {base}`, then `git commit -m "…"`, then push (if commits that must stay separate are mixed in, ask the user).{list}
push.squashPending: Counting the {pending} commit(s) this command makes, {branch} would have {n} commits not on any remote. Run the commit separately first, squash them (`git reset --soft {base}`, then `git commit -m "…"`), then push.{list}
answerLang.wrong: The last answer is not in {lang} (e.g. "{sample}"). This project answers in {lang}. Please rewrite that answer in {lang}.
checklist.start:
Checklist file for this session: {file}
For work with three or more steps, write "- [ ] task" lines here at the start and change finished ones to "- [x]". Add items when the user adds work. The hook shows the remaining items whenever the user sends a message.
docs.notDocWrite: Only documents (.md) and images (png, jpg, gif, svg, webp) go in {dir}/: {file}. Keep secrets, keys and notes outside the repository and mention only their location in the docs.
docs.notDoc: {file}: not a document (.md) or image. Move it out of docs/
docs.title: {file}: the first line must be `# Title`
docs.dateMissing: {file}: add a `> Last updated: {date} · one-line summary` line under the title
docs.dateOld: {file}: changed on {date} but the date line says {was} — update it
docs.noIndex: {file}: the index {index} is missing — create it and link this document
docs.notIndexed: {file}: add a link and a one-line description to the index {index}
docs.brokenLink: {index}: links to a document that does not exist → {file}
docs.stop:
Some documents do not follow the format. Fix them before finishing.
{list}
